stem: How did Sandra Day O’Connor contribute to the national identity of the United States?

options.label: A
options.text: She helped inspire women to seek careers in the judicial system.

options.label: B
options.text: Her election victory symbolized the dominance of women in politics.

options.label: C
options.text: Her judicial contributions led to the equal treatment of women in business.

options.label: D
options.text: She helped expose the mistreatment of women in their traditional roles.

visual_elements:
This time line shows select accomplishments of Sandra Day O’Connor.
Sandra Day O’Connor
1952 Graduates magna cum laude from Stanford Law School
1972 Becomes first woman to serve as a state senate majority leader while in Arizona
1981 Sworn in as the first female associate justice on the Supreme Court
1982 Writes an opinion that invalidates a women-only enrollment policy as reinforcing gender stereotypes
2005 Announces retirement from Supreme Court
2006 Law school at Arizona State University renamed the Sandra Day O’Connor College of Law
